QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p369/r17.claim: He returned to his family strutting with arrogance.

NAHHAS:v5p92/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r11.claim: He went away from obedience to God, treating the admonition lightly.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r11.anchor: أي ذهب معرضا عن طاعة الله جل وعز متهاونا بالموعظة

NAHHAS:v5p92/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r12.claim: Yatamatta is accusative as a circumstantial expression.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r12.anchor: و يتمطى في موضع نصب على الحال

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.claim: The passage describes denial of the fundamentals of faith, abandonment of prayer, and a swaggering return to family; the unbeliever merits blame and punishment for leaving prayer as for unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى شرح كيفية عمله فيما يتعلق بأصول الدين وبفروعه ، وفيما يتعلق بدنياه

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r4.claim: One etymology derives yatamaṭṭā from yatamaṭṭaṭ, “stretch,” since a swaggerer lengthens his strides; the consonants shifted as in taqaṣṣā from taqaṣṣaṣa.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r4.anchor: أن أصله يتمطط أي يتمدد ، لأن المتبختر يمد خطاه ، فقلبت الطاء فيه ياء

RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r5.claim: Another derives it from al-maṭā, the back, because the person twists his back; the cited report uses al-maṭīṭā for a swaggering gait.
RAZI-FULL:v30p205#3/r5.anchor: من المطا وهو الظهر لأنه يلويه ، وفي الحديث : ( إذا مشت أمتي المطيطي ) أي مشية المتبختر

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s third possibility is a divine command that Muhammad tell the enemy to beware, since an unbearable misfortune is near.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.anchor: أن يكون ذلك أمرا من الله لنبيه ، بأن يقولها لعدو الله ، فيكون المعنى { ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى } ( القيامة : 33 ) فقل له : يا محمد : { أولى لك فأولى } أي احذر

STUDYQURAN:75:33/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:33/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:33/r1.claim: This swaggering resembles mockers of the Prophet who winked at one another, returned blithely to their people, and called believers astray.
STUDYQURAN:75:33/r1.anchor: This verse is similar to 83:30–32, which says of those who would mock the Prophet: And when they passed them, they would wink at one another

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r1.claim: He went back to his family, strutting as he walked.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] أي يتبختر

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] أي يتبختر

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says he strutted, a gait associated with Banū Makhzūm.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: {ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] قال: يتبختر

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r4.claim: Mujāhid says Muhammad saw a Qurashī man walking and said that this man walked as the one in the verse did, strutting.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] قال: رأى رجلا من قريش يمشي

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies the strutting man as Abū Jahl ibn Hishām and says this was his characteristic gait.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله : {يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] قال: يتبختر وهو أبو جهل بن هشام

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r6.claim: Mujāhid identifies the strutting man as Abū Jahl.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {يتمطى} [القيامة: 33] قال: أبو جهل

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the passage is about Abū Jahl swaggering.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فلا صدق ولا صلى ولكن كذب وتولى ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى}

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r8.claim: The verb means twisting his back in a swagger; al-maṭā is the back.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r8.anchor: يلوي مطاه تبخترا، والمطا: هو الظهر

TAB-FULL:v23p524/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r9.claim: A Prophetic report criticizes the gait called al-muṭayṭāʾ, in which a man swings his arms and sways.
TAB-FULL:v23p524/r9.anchor: ومنه الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «وإذا مشت المطيطاء

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.claim: The pronouns refer to the human mentioned earlier; denied belief means affirming the Qur’an’s true call, and denied prayer is worship through salat, religion’s central pillar.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r1.anchor: الضمائر راجعة إلى الإنسان المذكور في قوله { أيحسب الإنسان } الخ

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r3.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r3.claim: Al-Majma‘ defines tamatti as stretching the body lazily, originally twisting or arching the back.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r3.anchor: والتمطي - على ما في المجمع - تمدد البدن من الكسل وأصله أن يلوي مطاه أي ظهره

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r4.claim: His strutting home is a metaphor for swaggering and arrogant pride.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r4.anchor: والمراد بتمطيه في ذهابه التبختر والاختيال استعارة

TABRISI:75:29-36/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:29-36/r12.claim: He returned to his family strutting and swaggering; the person intended is said to be Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r12.anchor: يرجع إليهم يتبختر ويختال في مشيته وقيل: إن المراد بذلك أبو جهل بن هشام

BURSEVI:v10p197/r19.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r19.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r19.claim: أهله may mean his household or his companions.

BURSEVI:v10p197/r20.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p197/r20.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p197/r20.claim: He walked swaggering and strutting proudly, boasting of his denial and turning away.
BURSEVI:v10p197/r20.anchor: يتبختر ويختال في مشيه افتخارا بذلك

BURSEVI:v10p198/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r1.claim: One derivation is from المط, stretching: the swaggerer lengthens his stride, so the word is a metaphor for strutting; its expected form يتمطط changes the last ط to ي to avoid identical adjacent consonants.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r1.anchor: من المط وهو المد فإن المتبختر يمد خطاه يعني أن التمدد في المشي من لوازم التبختر

BURSEVI:v10p198/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r2.claim: A second derivation takes it from المطا, the back: the strutter twists and moves his back, with the alif substituted for wāw.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r2.anchor: أو من المطا مقصورا وهو الظهر فإنه يلويه ويحركه في تبختره

BURSEVI:v10p198/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r3.claim: يتمطى is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ذهب.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r3.anchor: ويتمطى جمة حالية من فاعل ذهب

BURSEVI:v10p198/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r4.claim: The cited hadith uses المطيطاء for swaggering with an extended gait and arms; البأس means the severity of battle.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r4.anchor: التبختر ومد اليدين في المشي والبأص شدة الحرب

THALABI:v10p90/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p90/r8.claim: He went home strutting in pride.
THALABI:v10p90/r8.anchor: ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى يتبختر

THALABI:v10p90/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v10p90/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam calls it the gait of Banu Makhzum, deriving the word from the back and its proud twisting.
THALABI:v10p90/r9.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: هي مشية بني مخزوم وأصله من المطا وهو الظهر أي يلوي مطاه تبخترا

THALABI:v10p90/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r10.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p90/r10.claim: An alternative derives it from yatamattaṭu, “to stretch,” with one emphatic consonant changed into yāʾ; the word also describes stretching on rising from sleep.

THALABI:v10p90/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p90/r11.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p90/r11.claim: A report predicts that when the community walks with the strutting gait and serves Romans and Persians, God will set some people over others; Ibn Abi Najih explains al-muṭayṭaʾ by this verse.
THALABI:v10p90/r11.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا مشت أمتي المطيطاء وخدمتهم الروم وفارس سلط بعضهم على بعض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r1.claim: He denied the Qur’an, turned away from faith, and returned to his family.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولكن كذب}، أي: بالقرآن. {وتولى} عن الإيمان.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes explain yatematta as swaggering and walking arrogantly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r2.anchor: يتبختر ويختال في مشيته، (قاله ابن عباس (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r3.speaker: مقاتل، زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r3.claim: Muqatil and Zayd ibn Aslam call it the characteristic gait of Banu Makhzum.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬6)، وزيد بن أسلم (¬7): هو مشية بني مخزوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r4.claim: One derivation is from maṭw, stretching; the report says Abu Bakr passed Bilal stretching in the sun, and yatematta means to stretch oneself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r5.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r5.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj derive it from al-maṭā, the back: he twists his back in an arrogant gait.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء (¬3)، والزجاج (¬4): هو من المطا، وهو الظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة، ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn Qutayba derive it from al-maṭṭ, stretching; Ibn Qutayba explains a consonant shift from yatematta.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p525/r6.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة (¬7)، وابن قتيبة (¬8) في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r4.claim: He went back to his family strutting proudly.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r4.anchor: { ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى } يتبختر.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r6.claim: After this denial, he went back to his family, home, or town, proudly strutting and enjoying himself.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r6.anchor: Sonra da bununla iftihar ederek gerneşe gerneşe, kurula kurula ehline, evine veya iline keyif çatmaya gitti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r3.claim: Instead of listening and judging fairly, he turns away with blind bigotry, shuts his ears, and locks his heart.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r3.anchor: ilgi gösterip kulağını ve zihnini söylenenlere açacağı, insafla değerlendireceği yerde, kör bir taassupla gerçeğe sırtını döner, kulağını tıkar, kalbini kilitler.

FARRA:v3p211/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r12.claim: يتمطى means swaggering; المطا is the back, which the swaggerer twists, and the description refers specifically to Abu Jahl.
FARRA:v3p211/r12.anchor: يتبختر لأن الظهر هو المطا، فيلوي ظهره تبخترا وهذه خاصة في أبي جهل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r1.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means to swagger; its underlying form is yatamaṭṭaṭ, with ṭāʾ changed to yāʾ, like yataẓannā from yataẓannan, and the swaggering walk is called al-mashya al-miṭayṭāʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r1.anchor: {يتمطى} يتبختر. وأصله "يتمطط"؛ فقلبت الطاء فيه ياء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r2.claim: The ṭāʾ in this word ultimately comes from dāl: the underlying expression is that he extends his hand while swaggering; madd and maṭṭ have the same sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#3/r2.anchor: وأصل الطاء في هذا كله: دال. إنما هو: مد يده في المشي، إذا تبختر.

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r1.claim: يتمطى is a circumstantial clause whose subject is the subject of ذهب; it may also mean he began stretching himself.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r1.anchor: جملة حالية من فاعل " ذهب " ، وقد يجوز أن يكون بمعنى: شرع في التمطي

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r2.claim: One derivation takes تمطى from المطا, the back: he struts by extending and twisting his back as he walks.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أنه من المطا، والمطا: الظهر، ومعناه: يتبختر، أي: يمد مطاه ويلويه تبخترا في مشيته

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r3.claim: A second derivation is يتمطط, to stretch; it means stretching himself proudly as he walks, close in sense to the first but from a different root.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن أصله: يتمطط، من تمطط، أي: تمدد، ومعناه: أنه يتمدد في مشيته تبخترا

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r4.claim: On the second derivation, the third طاء becomes ياء to avoid three identical consonants; examples include تظنيت, قصيت أظفاري, and the cited line's تقضي.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r4.anchor: وإنما أبدلت الطاء الثالة ياء كراهة احتمال الأمثال نحو: تظنيت وقصيت أظفاري، وقوله: 4425 تقضي البازي

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r5.claim: المطيطاء means strutting and extending the arms while walking.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r5.anchor: والمطيطاء: التبختر ومد اليدين في المشي

SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r6.claim: المطيطة is thick water at the bottom of a basin, named because it stretches or spreads there.
SAMIN-DURR:75:33/r6.anchor: والمطيطة: الماء الخاثر أسفل الحوض؛ لأنه يتمطط، أي: يمتد فيه

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r3.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means strutting, derived from maṭā, the back.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r3.anchor: معناه بتبختر، مأخوذ من المطا وهو الظهر.

ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r3.claim: He then went arrogantly back to what he had come from.
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r3.anchor: went arrogantly back to what he had come from

ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n14/r1.claim: Asad glosses “to his people” as the arrogant belief rooted in social materialism; the note breaks off mid-phrase.
ASAD-NOTES:75:31#n14/r1.anchor: "to his people": i.e., to the arrogant belief, rooted in the materialism of his social

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r1.claim: Yatamatta means to strut, from maṭā (the back): the man twists his back in swagger.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r1.anchor: يتمطى، يتبختر وأصله من المطا، وهو الظهر، أي: يلوي مطاه تبختراً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r2.claim: An alternative derives the form from yatamaṭṭaṭ, ‘stretch out’; a doubled ṭāʾ becomes a weak letter to avoid repeated similars, as in taẓannā from taẓannan.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r2.anchor: وقيل أصله يتمطّط، أي: يتمدد في مشيته ومَدِّ منكبيه قلبت الطاء فيه حرفَ عِلَّة كراهة اجتماع الأمثال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r3.claim: His swaggering, back-twisting walk matches the fāqira that breaks the spine; this is a fitting punishment for the back he used to twist, better than a generic calamity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية مرتبطة بقوله تعالى: {تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ} . والفاقرة هي الداهية التي تقصم فقار الظهر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.claim: He once went home when he wished, but now is driven to his Lord and master against his will.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p226/r4.anchor: فهو كان يذهب إلى أهله وينقلب إليهم متى شاء، أما الآن فإنه يُساق سوقاً إلى ربه وسيده على الرغم من أَنْفِهِ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.claim: Worldly destinations were open, so the phrase was not fronted; now he is driven like a slave to one Lord, and fronting the destination signals no choice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r1.anchor: فليس ثمة حصر، ولذا لم يقدم الجار والمجرور في الدنيا، فقد كانت له فيها الحرية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.claim: The daily trip home needed no date, but his final being driven to the Lord occurs on the appointed day of departure; the contrasting phrases frame opposite scenes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r2.anchor: فإنه كان في الدنيا يذهب كل يوم وليس في يوم معيّن، أما سوقه إلى ربه فذلك في يوم معين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.claim: The Qiyāma figure is worse: unlike the possibly outwardly believing and praying people in Muhammad, he openly denies, turns away, then struts, so he deserves a stronger threat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r3.anchor: وربما أظهر الأول التصديق والصلاة في حين أن الثاني أظهر التكذيب والتولي، ثم ذهب إلى أهله متبختراً بذاك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r5.claim: When reminded of these duties, he responds with arrogance and walks away conceitedly to his family.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r5.anchor: he would be reminded of these duties, he would express utter arrogance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.claim: The disbelievers face an exacting journey without provisions: they neither prayed nor spent in God’s way, the two deeds that would benefit them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.anchor: no resources and provisions to take along.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r5.claim: A person whose wealth and children breed arrogance dismisses reminders and struts back to his family, treating prosperity as proof he is right and his poorer admonishers as mistaken.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r6.claim: Believers fear that they may fail their family and thereby incur God’s anger, as 52:26 says; this differs from the conceit of the people described here.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p83/r6.anchor: they will say: “we have always remained fearful in the matter of our family,”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r1.claim: The conceited see family as pride and good fortune: the orchard owner boasts it will never perish (18:35), and such people return to their families engrossed (83:31).
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r1.anchor: I don’t reckon that this will ever perish!

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r2.claim: The Qur’an also depicts these people returning to their families engrossed, in contrast to believers’ fearful sense of responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r2.anchor: when they would return to their people, they would return engrossed

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses “yatamaṭṭā” as swaggering and identifies the person as Abū Jahl.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ يتمطى ﴾ قال يقول يتبختر قال وهو أبو جهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r11.claim: أهله means his people or clan, and يتمطى means to strut proudly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r11.anchor: ثم ذهب إلى أهله: أي قومه، يتمطى: يبختر في مشيته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r1.claim: He went to his family swaggering proudly; such a person should fear God’s anger and walk humbly instead. ثم conveys remoteness or abhorrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r1.anchor: يتبختر افتخارا بذلك ومن صدر عنه مثل ذلك ينبغي أن يخاف من حلول غضب الله تعالى بهفيمشي خائفا متطامنا لا فرحا متبخترا فثم للأستبعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r2.claim: One derivation takes the word from stretching: a swaggerer lengthens his steps, and a doubled ط became a weak letter to avoid identical consonants, like تظني from تظنن.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r2.anchor: ويتمطى من المط فإن المتبختر يمد خطاه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, the word comes from the back: the swaggerer arches and stretches his back in pride.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r4.claim: A hadith warns that when the community walks in proud strutting and Persia and Rome serve them, their strength turns against one another and their worst rule their best.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r5.claim: Al-Tibi takes the clause as a wondrous contrast with the resurrection question: the man asks when it will come but prepares only for ruin; the intervening passage answers him, while the revelation instruction is a digression.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r5.anchor: وجعل الطيبيعطفهذه الجملة للتعجب على معنى يسأل أيان يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r11.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl, who belonged to Banu Makhzum and often swaggered in this way; another says the earlier “Does man think” passage also concerned him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r11.anchor: قومه بني مخزوم وكان يكثر منها ولم يبين حال العطف على هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r12.claim: Although the coordination is verbally distant, the author says its semantic distance is debatable: a general statement about humanity may still refer to Abu Jahl in one instance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p148#4/r12.anchor: نعم لا شك في بعد هذاالعطف لفظا لكنفي بعده معنى مقالولعل فيمابعد ما يقويجان بالعطفعلى ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r13.claim: He went back to his family, swaggering and strutting proudly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r13.anchor: ثم ذهب إلى أهله} رجع إليهم {يتمطى} يتبختر ويختال في مشيته،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r14.claim: The word may derive from تمطط, to stretch oneself; al-matt means extension.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r14.anchor: وقيل: أصله: "يتمطط" أي: يتمدد، والمط هو المد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r2.claim: He strutted in pride; the word may derive from stretching one's steps, originally y atamaṭṭaṭ, or from matt, “back,” referring to twisting it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r2.anchor: فإن المتبختر يمد خطاه فيكون أصله يتمطط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r1.claim: The denier goes home unconcerned with the consequences and flaunts his rejection; indulgence corrupted his practical and intellectual faculties until indifference became an ingrained vice he boasts about.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r1.anchor: أي هذا الإنسان بعد توليه عن الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r2.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means swaggering in pride; it is linked either to stretching the back and stride or to twisting the back while strutting, instead of showing shame and humility.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r2.anchor: أي يفتخر افتخارا بتكذيبه وإعراضه وعدم مبالاته بذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.claim: Qatadah identifies the denier as Abu Jahl: he did not affirm God’s Book or pray, rejected it, turned from obedience, and went home swaggering.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فلا صدق}

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r9.claim: Mujahid says the swaggering man is Abu Jahl, strutting as he went home.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} قال: يتبختر وهو أبو جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yatamaṭṭā as swaggering.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {يتمطى} قال: يختال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses yatamaṭṭā as strutting proudly.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3389#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يتمطى قال : يختال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r7.claim: يتمطى means walking with المطياطى, that is, swaggering and strutting.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r8.claim: The form derives from يتمطط, to stretch out: the swaggerer lengthens his steps, walking in self-admiration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p362/r8.anchor: وأصل { يتمطى } : يتمطط ، أي يتمدد لأن المتبختر يمد خطاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the strutting detail nearly identifies Abu Jahl outright because the gait was characteristic of Banu Makhzum and Abu Jahl often used it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ثم كادت هذه الآية أن تصرح له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r5.claim: يتمطى means walking in a strutting gait; Zayd ibn Aslam says it was Banu Makhzum's style, derived from the back because the body sways.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r5.anchor: ويتمطى معناه يمشي المطيطى وهي مشية بتبختر قال زيد بن أسلم: كانت مشية بني مخزوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r6.claim: The Prophet warned that when his community struts and Romans and Persians serve them, God will set some of them over others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r6.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا مشت أمتي المطيطى وخدمتهم الروم وفارس سلط بعضهم على بعض»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r1.claim: He returned to his family strutting and swaggering.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r2.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means to swagger; al-matā is the back, which the strutting person twists.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r2.anchor: قال الفراء يتمطى أي يتبختر لأن الظهر هو المطا فيلوي ظهره متبخترا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r3.claim: The form derives from yatamaṭṭaṭ, with ṭāʾ turned into yāʾ, as in yatadhannā from yatadhannan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أصله يتمطط فقلبت الطاء فيه ياء كما قيل يتظنى واصله يتظنن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r4.claim: The related gait is al-muṭayṭāʾ; its root originally has dāl and describes extending the hand while walking in a swagger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r4.anchor: ومنه المشية المطيطاء واصل الطاء في هذا كله دال إنما هو مد يده في المشي إذا تبختر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#4/r5.claim: The verb maṭaṭtu can mean extended, as does madadtu.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r3.claim: He goes home gloating, insolent, conceited, and lazy, lacking purpose or work; Ibn Kathir compares this with the descriptions in al-Mutaffifin and al-Inshiqaq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r3.anchor: أشرا بطرا كسلانا، لا همة له ولا عمل، كما قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by al-Dahhak, glosses the man's gait as swaggering or strutting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى} [أي] (3) . يختال.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وزيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r5.claim: Qatada and Zayd ibn Aslam explain yata-matta as walking boastfully or swaggering.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة، وزيد بن أسلم: يتبختر.

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r10.claim: Tamattī means stretching one's belly from laziness; it comes from madd, and the form yamattaṭu changed one emphatic tāʾ into yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r10.anchor: والتمطي: تمدد البطن عن الكسل، والمط: المد

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r11.claim: Another etymology derives the word from yalwī maṭāhu, twisting his back, with maṭā meaning the back.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r11.anchor: وقيل: أصله: يلوى مطاه، والمطا: الظهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r4.claim: يتمطى means strutting, from تتمطط, to stretch, because a strutter lengthens his steps.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, it derives from المطا, the back, which the strutter twists.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو من المطا وهو الظهر ، لأنه يلويه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r6.claim: A hadith says that when the community walks arrogantly and Persians and Romans serve them, their strength turns against one another.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r6.anchor: إذا مشت أمتى المطيطاء وخدمتهم فارس والروم فقد جعل بأسهم بينهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r23.claim: The person strutting off to his family is Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r23.anchor: يعني أبا جهل ، وفيه ثلاثة أوجه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r24.claim: Yatamatta means that he was conceited in himself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r24.anchor: يختال في نفسه ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r25.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r25.claim: It means walking with a swagger, described as the gait of Banu Makhzum.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r25.anchor: يتبختر في مشيته ، قال زيد بن أسلم وهي مشية بني مخزوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r26.claim: A third explanation derives it from bending one’s back, since al-mata means the back.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r27.claim: The text notes a prohibition on the gait called al-matitaa, in which a man swings his hands while walking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r27.anchor: وجاء النهي عن مشية المطيطاء وذلك أن الرجل يلقي يديه مع الكفين في مشيه

MUQATIL:75:22-33/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r12.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means to strut; the Banu al-Mughira strutted as they walked.
MUQATIL:75:22-33/r12.anchor: { ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى } [آية: 33] يقول: يتبختر، وكذلك بنو المغيرة بن عبدالله ابن عمر المخزومي إذا مشى أحدهم يختال في المشي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r1.claim: “يتمطى” means strutting; its original form is “يتمطط”, meaning to stretch, since a swaggerer lengthens his stride.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r1.anchor: يتبختر واصله يتمطط أي يتمدد لأن المتبختر يمد خطاه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r2.claim: The tāʾ changed to yāʾ to avoid three identical letters meeting.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#10/r2.anchor: فابدات الطاء ياء لاجتماع ثلاثة أحرف متماثلة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r2.claim: Mujahid and others call the return home an arrogant strut; Mujahid identifies the man as Abu Jahl.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r2.anchor: قاله مجاهد وغيره. مجاهد: المراد به أبو جهل

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r3.claim: One explanation derives yamatta from al-matā, the back, and means twisting the back.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r3.anchor: وقيل: «يتمطى» من المطا وهو الظهر، والمعنى يلوي مطاه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r4.claim: Another derives it from yatomattaṭ, lazy or heavy stretching; ṭāʾ became yāʾ to avoid doubling, conveying disregard and arrogance.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r4.anchor: وقيل: أصله يتمطط، وهو التمدد من التكسل والتثاقل، فهو يتثاقل عن الداعي

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r5.claim: Qurtubi explains the strut as stretching and twisting the back; al-muṭīṭa is thick water at a basin’s bottom because it stretches.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r5.anchor: والتمطي يدل على قلة الاكتراث، وهو التمدد، كأنه يمد ظهره ويلويه من التبختر

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r6.claim: An unattributed report warns that when the community walks in al-muṭayṭāʾ and Persians and Romans serve them, their strife will be among themselves; the term means swaggering with arms extended.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r6.anchor: والمطيطاء: التبختر ومد اليدين في المشي

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.claim: The four faults are failure to believe the Messenger, failure to pray before God, denial, and turning away from prayer; strutting predated denial.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.anchor: فترك التصديق خصلة، والتكذيب خصلة، وترك الصلاة خصلة، والتولي عن الله تعالى خصلة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r9.claim: Qatada explains that swaggering home was the man’s prior habit, so it is not a fifth fault.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r9.anchor: فإنا نقول: تلك كانت عادته قبل التكذيب والتولي
